newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Second letter bomb found at United Nations.
newsitem.headline: Second letter bomb found at United Nations.

text.p: United Nations security personnel on Monday afternoon found a second letter bomb at U.N. headquarters and called in New York City bomb squads to dismantle it, spokesman Fred Eckhard said.

"It was similar to the one this morning," Eckhard said, referring to a letter bomb discovered earlier in the day and addressed to the U.N. bureau of the Arabic-language newspaper Al-Hayat. But he said he could not confirm the second one was also addressed to Al-Hayat.

After the first suspicious envelope was discovered in a messenger room at U.N. headquarters, parts of two floors of the 38-story complex were closed off and the New York police bomb squad was called in. Other suspicious envelopes were found but on inspection they did not contain bomb materials.
Late in the afternoon Eckhard said the bomb squad had been called into a U.N. basement where mail was sorted to dismantle another letter bomb. He gave no further details.
The bomb discovered on Monday morning and address to Al-Hayat bore an Alexandria, Egypt, postmark, according to sources at the United Nations.
Earlier on Monday a letter bomb exploded at Al-Hayat's London office, wounding two security guards. Four more suspect devices were subsequently found there, British police said.
